title: Ultrafast X-ray-induced dephasing of valence electrons
authors: J. Vonka, B. Pedrini, J. Ravnik, A. Steppke, E. Prat, S. Reiche, D. G. Mazzone, P. Anand, S. Allenspach, Y. Ekinci, U. Staub, S. -W. Huang, M. Sander, R. Mankowsky, H. T. Lemke, G. Aeppli, S. Gerber
abstract: Diffract-before-destroy schemes for atomic-scale electron mapping assume that ultrashort X-ray pulses outrun radiation damage. Although atomic cores move over tens of femtoseconds, outer electrons respond much faster, compromising their locations. We test this limit in elemental silicon using broadband, energy-chirped X-ray pulses to encode time with few-femtosecond resolution. Comparing valence-sensitive structurally forbidden reflections with simultaneously measured core-dominated Bragg peaks reveals valence-bond dephasing on sub-20-fs timescales even at pulse energies where direct ionization effects are negligible. Our findings demonstrate that crystallography where outer electrons contribute substantially to Bragg peaks requires pulses shorter than today's standard $\sim50\,fs$ standard. They also establish a path to disentangle valence electron and lattice contributions to order and dynamics with hard X-rays, enabling studies across molecular biology, quantum matter and devices.
summary:
- Valence electrons in silicon dephase within <20 fs under ultrafast X‑ray pulses, even when core ionization is minimal.
- Broadband, chirped X‑ray pulses provide few‑fs time encoding, showing outer‑electron dynamics outrun atomic core motion.
- Crystallographic studies relying on valence contributions require pulses shorter than ~50 fs, enabling separation of valence and lattice dynamics.

title: The Virasoro Bootstrap: from the $c\sim1$ desert to coupled Potts
authors: Stefanos R. Kousvos, Alessandro Piazza, Alessandro Vichi
abstract: We develop a numerical conformal bootstrap for two-dimensional CFTs with $c>1$ based on Virasoro conformal blocks, computed with Zamolodchikov's recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation. As a first test we isolate an island around three decoupled Ising models. We then consider three 3-state Potts models coupled through their energy operators, a candidate irrational CFT. Mixed correlators isolate the decoupled theory in an island, and different gap assumptions, motivated by perturbation theory, yield a peninsula that contains the coupled fixed point but not the decoupled one. Finally, we explore the standard single-correlator bound on the lowest-dimension scalar primary in the OPE of two identical scalars. We find that for central charges just above $c=1$ the bound collapses over a wide range of external dimensions. This excludes any theory whose lightest scalar is absent from its own OPE and lies in this range, and supports the conjecture that no compact CFT exists in this region. We explain several features of these bounds analytically.
summary:
- Developed a 2D bootstrap for \(c>1\) using Virasoro blocks via Zamolodchikov recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation.
- Isolated islands for three decoupled Ising models and a peninsula containing the coupled 3‑state Potts fixed point using mixed correlators.
- Found that single‑correlator bounds collapse just above \(c=1\), ruling out theories without a lightest scalar in their OPE and supporting the absence of compact CFTs in that region.

title: An Intrinsically Gapless Topological Phase with Dipole Symmetry
authors: Amogh Anakru, Linhao Li, Zhen Bi
abstract: We show that the boundary fractionalization familiar from gapped topological insulators can enforce bulk gaplessness in a dipole-conserving system. In a one-dimensional fermion model with charge conservation, dipole conservation, and particle-hole symmetry, we realize an intrinsically gapless symmetry-protected topological (igSPT) phase combining a dipolar Luttinger liquid with half-quantized boundary charges. This boundary structure obstructs a unique gapped bulk preserving these symmetries and lattice translation. Remarkably, the two charge-neutral edge configurations remain exactly degenerate even at finite size due to dipole conservation and particle-hole symmetry. The boundary fractionalization also manifests as shifted conformal towers in the dipole-resolved entanglement spectrum, reflecting distinct conformal boundary conditions of the Luttinger liquid. We support our analysis of the igSPT by studying exactly-solvable limits and performing DMRG computations, establishing its stability for a wide range of tuning parameters.
summary:
- Boundary fractionalization in a dipole‑conserving 1D fermion model forces bulk gaplessness, creating an intrinsically gapless SPT (igSPT).
- The phase hosts a dipolar Luttinger liquid with half‑quantized boundary charges; edge configurations stay exactly degenerate at finite size due to dipole and particle‑hole symmetry.
- Dipole‑resolved entanglement spectra exhibit shifted conformal towers, indicating distinct conformal boundary conditions, confirmed by solvable limits and DMRG.

title: Theory of the Ferroaxial Charge Density Wave in 1T-TiSe$_2$
authors: Ilaria Maccari, Rafael M. Fernandes, Fernando de Juan, Maria N. Gastiasoro
abstract: Recent experiments using strain to probe the charge-density wave (CDW) of 1T-TiSe$_2$ have uncovered additional transitions and broken symmetries inside the CDW state. The elastocaloric effect reveals a second transition below $T_\mathrm{CDW}$, which elastoresistivity shows to be associated with ferroaxial order, breaking all vertical mirror symmetries while preserving inversion. In addition, at even lower temperatures, a diverging nematic susceptibility has been reported through elastoresistivity. In this work, we argue that this rich phenomenology cannot be explained by the standard $L_1^-$ CDW order parameter, and instead requires the existence of a secondary CDW order parameter. Based on symmetry, microscopic, and diffraction considerations, we propose this subleading CDW to have $L_2^-$ symmetry. By analyzing the Landau theory of coupled $L_1^-$ and $L_2^-$ orders in the presence of strain, we reproduce the phase boundaries observed in the elastocaloric measurements and the emergence of ferroaxial order below the CDW transition. Moreover, the model supports a third threefold-rotational symmetry breaking transition at lower temperatures, consistent with the reported divergence of the nematic susceptibility.
summary:
- Proposes a secondary \(L_2^-\) CDW order to account for ferroaxial and nematic transitions in 1T‑TiSe₂.
- Landau theory with strain reproduces elastocaloric phase boundaries and ferroaxial symmetry breaking.
- Predicts a third threefold‑rotational symmetry breaking transition, matching the diverging nematic susceptibility.

title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
abstract: The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the Rényi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. At an index $n_*$ its charged operator merges with its alternate-quantization partner, and the defect loses conformality. Beyond $n_*$ it flows with no source to a conformal defect that breaks the U(1) symmetry; below $n_*$ that defect needs a symmetry-breaking source, so at large $N$, conformality loss makes the breaking spontaneous. The scalar hair beyond $n_*$, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, thus preserves them outside a thin layer at the entangling surface, as conformal symmetry requires. The region outside the layer sets the universal term of the Rényi entropy. We demonstrate the mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, where the saddles are in closed form and numerical methods confirm the flows. On a sphere we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the sphere is large enough; it is then unique and ends at the symmetry-breaking defect. The mechanism needs a scalar mass in a finite window, and for potentials attractive at small amplitude, the symmetry can break before conformality is lost. For operators of low enough dimension, already the second Rényi entropy lies beyond the merger. Classical backreaction does not move the merger at any order; we argue that away from $n_*$ the flows persist at first order.
summary:
- Rényi defect loses conformality at a critical index \(n_*\) when a charged operator merges with its alternate‑quantization partner.
- For \(n>n_*\) the defect flows to a source‑free, symmetry‑breaking conformal defect; for \(n<n_*\) a symmetry‑breaking source is required, making the breaking spontaneous at large \(N\).
- The mechanism is explicitly realized in the probe Abelian‑Higgs model on AdS\(_5\) (Bogomolny point), with unique, source‑free flows on large spheres and a scalar mass window that preserves the merger under backreaction.

title: From photons to fractons: Casimir effect in higher-rank electrodynamics and its fractonic branch
abstract: The Casimir effect probes the modes that can propagate between boundaries. This makes it useful for fracton gauge theories, where restricted mobility follows from the simultaneous conservation of charge and dipole moment and changes the physical sector of the theory. We compare ordinary Maxwell electrodynamics with a Lorentz-covariant higher-rank theory of a symmetric tensor gauge field and with the scalar-charge fractonic branch selected from it by a preferred timelike background. The comparison shows why the distinction matters. In the full covariant theory, the Euclidean slab problem contains three independently propagating Maxwell-like modes and two coupled vector sectors that do not reduce to independent ordinary modes. Their boundary determinants are well defined, but a Lorentzian analysis shows that the vector sector has an unbounded Hamiltonian, so these determinants do not describe the vacuum energy of a stable fractonic phase. On the fractonic branch, the Gauss constraint removes that vector sector and leaves three stable massless modes: two transverse-traceless tensor modes and one scalar trace mode. For ideal reflectors, the physical Casimir energy is therefore 3/2 of the corresponding Maxwell result, for both equal and complementary boundary conditions. The calculation isolates the effect of the fractonic restriction on the radiative spectrum and clarifies which features of the full higher-rank boundary problem survive in the physical fracton sector.
summary:
- Three stable massless modes (2 TT tensors + 1 scalar) remain after imposing the fractonic Gauss constraint, giving a Casimir energy 3/2 that of Maxwell for ideal reflectors.
- The full Lorentz‑covariant theory contains an unstable vector sector with an unbounded Hamiltonian, so its boundary determinants do not describe a stable vacuum.
- The analysis isolates how the fractonic restriction removes the unstable sector and preserves only the physical radiative spectrum.

title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
authors: Sayantan Dey, Abel Carreras, Siddhartha Patra
abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.
summary:
- Entanglement in spin SYK‑dot chains is bounded by ⌊p/2⌋ ln 2 plus inter‑dot terms, limiting tensor‑network and quantum simulation efficiency.
- Quantum advantage appears only for dots ≈15–21 qubits, demanding two‑qubit error rates ≈10⁻⁶, beyond NISQ reach.
- MPS and variational circuit tests confirm the entanglement bound, energy convergence, and fidelity decay predictions.

title: Enforced Gaplessness by Combining Non-Anomalous Symmetries
abstract: Symmetry-enforced gaplessness is a phenomenon in which a quantum system is forced to be gapless due to its global symmetry. Previous works have mainly focused on anomalous symmetries. Another approach, using symmetry spans, which specify two embeddings of a common symmetry into two larger symmetries, was proposed by the authors. In this work, we show that a symmetry span can enforce gaplessness even when both larger symmetries are invertible and non-anomalous: each alone admits a trivially gapped phase, but because the embeddings differ by a twist associated with a symmetry-protected topological phase, the symmetry they generate admits no gapped phase with finitely many ground states. We present such a span of a finite group and $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$ in 1+1 dimensions, with continuum realizations and a lattice Hamiltonian, with a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space and finitely many parameters, that is gapless in any region of its parameter space. We also discuss a 2+1-dimensional example and spans of only finite symmetries.
summary:
- Symmetry spans of two embeddings of a common symmetry into larger non‑anomalous groups can enforce gaplessness.
- A 1+1D lattice model with a finite‑dimensional local Hilbert space (finite group ↔ U(²) is gapless for all parameter values.
- The paper also presents a 2+1D example and discusses spans involving only finite symmetries.

title: Hidden variable $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet
authors: Hao Tian, Pengwei Zhao, Gang v. Chen
abstract: Topological orders in realistic systems are quite rare, raising one fundamental question of whether they might be harbored with hidden degrees of freedom rather than directly exposed in conventional spins or electrons. We here propose a set of hidden variables and their effective interactions in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet. By properly organizing four local states of the spin dimer into two pseudospin-$1/2$ variables ($\boldsymbolτ$ and $\boldsymbolμ$), we identify a regime where an effective Balents-Fisher-Girvin model emerges, realizing a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order in the hidden $\boldsymbolτ$ sector while the auxiliary $\boldsymbolμ$ sector remains a trivial paramagnet. This hidden nature drastically alters the experimental manifestations. Physical spins map to composite objects, typically convolving fractionalized anyon continua with non-topological magnon excitations. Nevertheless, specific symmetry-selected channels, such as the longitudinal intralayer response, exclusively reveal the bare two-vison continuum without collective-mode dressing. Our findings demonstrate that the topological order could be buried in certain hidden and emergent degrees of freedom, pointing to a promising pathway for seeking elusive topological states disguised within hidden internal degrees of freedom.
summary:
- Hidden $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order appears in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet via pseudospin-$1/2$ variables $\tau$ (topological) and $\mu$ (trivial).
- Physical spin signals mix fractionalized anyon continua with ordinary magnons, obscuring the topological order except in symmetry‑selected probes.
- The longitudinal intralayer response uniquely reveals the bare two‑vison continuum, offering a clear experimental fingerprint.

title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
authors: M. Cristina Diamantini, Carlo A. Trugenberger
abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.
summary:
- Superinsulation is a quantum phase dual to superconductivity, where U(electromagnetic fields become confining.
- In granular superconductors, tensionless XY vortices liberate magnetic monopoles that condense, forming magnetic flux tubes that confine electric fields into linear potentials between Cooper pairs.
- The resulting infinite resistance persists until a finite deconfinement temperature, with experiments confirming the linear confining potential and challenging phase‑only/disorder models.
